content.text: Intent

Give the firm a single register of the counterparties it does business with — banks, corporates and funds — with each counterparty's legal name, short code, type, lifecycle status, credit limit, onboarding date, sanctions-screening flag, registered address and contacts. Anyone signed in can browse and maintain the register; the table's uniqueness and immutability rules keep the register clean as it grows.
Scope

IN: the Counterparty entity with its embedded PostalAddress and Contact beans, its search screen and edit form, and the lifecycle draft → active → retired (draft → active → retired, retired terminal).

IN: retirement is a state of the register, not a behavioural gate at this stage — a retired counterparty may still be edited and may still be picked as another counterparty's parent; its status is the only thing that changes.
OUT (non-goals): sanctions screening itself (the register only records that it happened, via
sanctionsScreened
), credit-limit workflow or approval, legal agreements and trades against a counterparty, and any integration to an external legal-entity identifier service.
Scenarios
None — the bean's standard screens cover the journeys (create, edit, browse, retire); no ordered process beyond them is in scope.
Requirements
P1: A counterparty is never its own ancestor — the
parent
chain is acyclic.
R1: WHEN a counterparty's
status

is changed, the system SHALL accept the change only along the transition graph draft → active → retired, with retired terminal — and SHALL reject every other transition, including draft → retired and any change out of retired.

Note (framing, not a requirement): every other rule — legalName and shortCode uniqueness, shortCode immutability, the type and status vocabularies, the creditLimit floor, the defaults — is carried by the bean table and enforced and tested by the platform.
Data model
bean: Counterparty
Relationships:
parent
is a self-reference to another Counterparty (optional — a counterparty may be at the top of its group).
registeredAddress
and
contacts
are embedded, so they live and die with their counterparty. Beyond the table: the parent chain must stay acyclic (P1).
bean: PostalAddress
Embedded only — never persisted on its own.
bean: Contact
Embedded only — never persisted on its own.
User interface
The Counterparty search screen and edit form. The form edits the embedded registered address and contacts inline, in place, as part of the one row.
Dependencies

None — no existing entity, registered spec or external system is relied on; the register is new ground (the reuse gate found no counterparty entity among the 61 live entities and no overlapping spec).
Constraints
Considered, none apply: authorization (any signed-in user, the platform's default), performance, volume, availability, audit, privacy, locale, cost.
Acceptance criteria
A1 (verifies P1): WHEN a counterparty's
parent
is set to the counterparty itself, or directly or through a chain to one of its own descendants, the system SHALL reject the change and leave the parent chain unchanged.
A2 (verifies R1): WHEN a counterparty in status draft is set to active, or one in active is set to retired, the system SHALL accept the change.

A3 (verifies R1): WHEN a counterparty's status is set to any transition other than draft → active or active → retired — draft → retired, active → draft, retired → draft, or retired → active — the system SHALL reject the change and leave the status unchanged.
Migration & compatibility
None — new entity, nothing to migrate; no existing rows, users or callers are affected.
Artifacts
A Counterparty register: the Counterparty entity (with its embedded PostalAddress and Contact beans), its search screen and its edit form.
Derived from the Data model
Implied by the bean blocks in the Data model and regenerated by the platform - do not edit this block; author above it what the catalog cannot derive.

Counterparty - persistence.entity (persistence): The entity class with its builder, its descriptor + jsontype entry, its migration and table, and its tests; the descriptor is authored at spec time as the bean's entity-descriptor attachment (entity_descriptors/{qualified-descriptor-name}.json).
Counterparty - observer.sheet (observer): The observer sheet: the entity's only remote surface, reads and writes.

Counterparty - ui.defaultForm (ui): The default form of one row, rendered wherever the row is viewed or edited: its layout JS, authored at spec time as the spec's ui/{qualified-descriptor-name}.js attachment and shipped beside the entity class.
Counterparty.legalName - validation.rule (persistence): unique - enforced on save and covered by a generated test
Counterparty.shortCode - validation.rule (persistence): unique - enforced on save and covered by a generated test
Counterparty.shortCode - validation.rule (persistence): immutable - enforced on save and covered by a generated test
Counterparty.status - validation.rule (persistence): default(draft) - enforced on save and covered by a generated test
Counterparty.creditLimit - validation.rule (persistence): min(0) - enforced on save and covered by a generated test
Counterparty.sanctionsScreened - validation.rule (persistence): default(false) - enforced on save and covered by a generated test

PostalAddress - embeddedBean (bean): A bean another bean embeds: its class with its builder, its descriptor + jsontype entry and its tests - a plain bean with NO persistence descriptor, so no migration, no table and no sheet; it lives inside the row of the bean that embeds it, and its descriptor is authored at spec time as its entity-descriptor attachment (entity_descriptors/{qualified-descriptor-name}.json).

PostalAddress - ui.defaultForm (ui): The default form of one row, rendered wherever the row is viewed or edited: its layout JS, authored at spec time as the spec's ui/{qualified-descriptor-name}.js attachment and shipped beside the entity class.

Contact - embeddedBean (bean): A bean another bean embeds: its class with its builder, its descriptor + jsontype entry and its tests - a plain bean with NO persistence descriptor, so no migration, no table and no sheet; it lives inside the row of the bean that embeds it, and its descriptor is authored at spec time as its entity-descriptor attachment (entity_descriptors/{qualified-descriptor-name}.json).

Contact - ui.defaultForm (ui): The default form of one row, rendered wherever the row is viewed or edited: its layout JS, authored at spec time as the spec's ui/{qualified-descriptor-name}.js attachment and shipped beside the entity class.
Open Questions
None — the data model was declared final by the author and no business decision is left open.
